messages:
anya_support: Hey team — customer (AcmeCD) says their latest invoice has 720 reserved GPU hours billed but our Dedicated dashboard shows only ~540 hours consumed for the billing period. They want a clear breakdown before payment dispute.

devon_billing: Thanks for flagging. Do we have the invoice line items? Is that 720 billed as 'Reserved Capacity (hours)' or something else?

billing-bot: Invoice 2026-03-01_87321: 
- Reserved Capacity: 720 hours @ $X/hr
- Burst Usage: 190 hours @ $Y/hr
- Credits/SLA Adjustments: $0
(note: invoice_time: 2026-03-01T00:00Z)

anya_support: Customer pasted that exact invoice snippet. Their Dedicated dashboard -> "Reserved Pool Usage" graph maxes at ~540h for period Mar 1–31. They also say their app never used burst routing explicitly.

liam_sre: A few things to check: 1) timezone/period alignment (invoice might be UTC vs dashboard local), 2) whether hours are billed per provisioned node vs effective usage (we bill reserved hours for provisioned vGPU instances even if idle), 3) pooled vs per-tenant attribution.

devon_billing: Right — dedicated model: we bill committed hours for the pool (reserved capacity), not necessarily token-level usage. If AcmeCD booked a 24/7 1-GPU reservation for 30 days: 24*30 = 720h. Dashboard showing 540h might be per-tenant consumption if they moved some capacity to a team or had downtime.

anya_support: Customer insists they de-provisioned for ~7 days (scheduled maintenance) and expected billed hours to be reduced accordingly — they thought reserved billing pauses on de-provision. Is that true?

liam_sre: For Dedicated Reserved, billing is for the committed capacity hours in the contract. De-provisioning a model or instances in the console does NOT reduce reserved billing unless they reduce the reservation or use burst credits policies configured.

devon_billing: Confirming. Only changes to the reserved contract (canceled or changed reservation) will alter billed reserved hours. However, we should verify the invoice didn't also include burst charges or redirected billing for failover regions.

maria_account_mgr: I'll pull the contract / reservation record for AcmeCD. Can someone run a query to show pool-level allocation and any failover routing for that period? Query should include: pool_id, provisioned_vgpus, start_ts, end_ts, region, attributed_tenant_hours.

liam_sre: Running quick audit now. Snippet: 
```
SELECT pool_id, sum(provisioned_hours) as pool_hours, sum(attributed_hours) as tenant_hours
FROM dedicated_usage
WHERE pool_id = 'pool-acme-01' AND ts >= '2026-03-01' AND ts < '2026-04-01'
GROUP BY pool_id;
```
Result: pool_hours = 720, tenant_hours (sum of attributed tenants) = 540.

anya_support: So pool was provisioned full-time (720h) while AcmeCD only used 540h worth of work (other 180h were idle or served other tenants?)

devon_billing: Exactly. Invoice is for the reservation (pool_hours). The dashboard view the customer looked at is likely the "tenant_attributed_usage" view, which shows only attributed processing time. We should explain difference and include a line-by-line mapping.

anya_support: Customer asked for evidence — can we produce a short exported csv showing pool-level provisioning timeline + attributed hours per tenant for the month? Also need a clear explanation sentence they can send to finance.

liam_sre: I'll export: columns: ts_start, ts_end, provisioned_vgpus, pool_hours_segment, tenant_id, attributed_hours_segment, routing_reason. Will include routing_reason values: idle, tenant_run, failover, maintenance. For this month there's a maintenance window Mar 10–16 where the pool was provisioned but marked idle -> contributes to pool_hours but attributed_hours = 0 for AcmeCD.

devon_billing: Also double-check burst credits: their plan includes 200 burst hours/month. Invoice shows 190 burst hours charged — that aligns with tenant attributed > pool spare capacity during spikes. But not relevant to reserved-hour difference.

maria_account_mgr: I'll message the customer with: 1) explanation of reservation billing model, 2) attached CSV export, 3) note on how to reduce future reserved billing (downgrade reservation or schedule capacity reduction on contract). Any objections?

anya_support: Sounds good. One more ask from customer: they want SLA credit for the maintenance downtime Mar 10–16 because they claim service was impacted. Did we issue any SLA credits?

liam_sre: SLA credit pipeline: I see a ticket open but no credit applied. We need to verify SLA violation windows: their SLA is uptime >= 99.9 for Dedicated. The maintenance window was scheduled (customer notified?) — scheduled maintenance is excluded unless unscheduled or SLA hit. Need to check notification logs.

devon_billing: If SLA credit is warranted, billing team applies a negative line item. For now invoice shows $0 credits. We'll wait for postmortem outcome.

anya_support: I'll bundle the CSV and plain-English breakdown and send to AcmeCD now, and CC account manager. Tagging @maria_account_mgr for contract change steps.

maria_account_mgr: On it — will also share options: pause reserved hours (requires contract amendment), convert to dedicated autoscale (lower base reservation + burst), or add rollover for unused reserved hours (requires legal/finance signoff).

anya_support: Thanks everyone. Follow-up: if customer escalates to dispute, route to finance with exported pool -> tenant mapping + contract excerpt. Closing thread after I send message. :white_check_mark:
